body:
Timed host `load_blob` and `scatter` writes share the Goldcrest timing and
bandwidth resources used by hardware AXI traffic. With `ddr_timing` omitted or
false, initialization stays on the immediate backdoor. With it enabled, writes
use the existing CMN-egress XMS AXI masters: independent operations overlap,
overlapping bytes retain source order, and later commands wait for responses.
The driver preserves the earliest failed operation even when errors arrive out
of order, and warns when later already-issued writes may have modified memory.
Untimed programs install no timed-driver callbacks. The driver is created on
first timed use and retained across groups. Timed groups reuse the bounded
command iterator; buffer refills do not drain outstanding transfers.

XMS routing, arbitration, buffering and clock crossings execute in RTL. The
host handles address mapping, partial strobes, outstanding IDs and completion.
Decode-mode reads use the XCP CSR at `0x20020B08 + pair*0x1000`, with HRA writes
invalidating the mapping cache. The modeled path starts at CMN egress; CPU
execution, coherence and earlier CMN scheduling are outside its boundary.

The 32 embedded datapath lanes restore tunable defaults on every lane reset:
61 AXI cycles of read latency, 40 cycles of posted write-response latency,
63 outstanding reads/writes, about 38.4 GB/s shared read/write service per lane
and 42.1875 GB/s per direction at a 1 GHz AXI clock. Periodic refresh pauses
default off and remain programmable. These are optimistic engineering estimates
based on x32 LPDDR5X at 9.6 GT/s, a 40 ns remote round trip and a 21 ns row-hit
read component. Exact DRAM organization, channel mapping and controller policy
remain uncalibrated; detailed bank/row scheduling is not modeled.

Cadence AVIP supplies READY, response-latency, burst-gap and request-limit
controls. The wrapper adds shared/directional byte-rate scheduling, optional
refresh pauses, read buffering, accounting and reset support. Host
`goldcrest_timing` settings program these controls through staging and MARG.
Omitted settings perform no timing-bank access and impose no initialization
requirement. Programs with overrides must begin with `load_blob` targeting
`serial_config` and use release-all boot (TWS/SPM/XMS/HRA released together).
The host applies overrides only after that initializer succeeds, reusing its
existing reset-readiness wait and settle interval, before subsequent operations.
The package tool, stager and executor reject missing or misordered initialization.
Overrides are validated against the resident profile, programmed and read back.
Every later lane reset requires reapplication. Updates require drained AXI traffic
and stable reset; a partial programming failure requires reset and reapplication
before traffic. There is no custom readiness marker, reset watchdog or
fresh-profile tracking. The offline structural dry-run accepts timing profiles
and consumes timed-write payloads in bounded chunks while preserving source and
read failures; it does not model DDR timing or hardware reset readiness.

Explicit zero delays and service bypass remain supported. AUX and unindexed FC
instances retain native behavior without the added timing-control processes or
MARG maps. The scheduler and lane-service modules have separate source files,
with HEMI/FC and focused-test filelists wired explicitly. The preexisting
real-Goldcrest generator is unchanged. Timing-control indices are named without
changing the memory-bank layout or reset values. An ordinary model rebuild is
required; no timing build switch or TEL dependency is added.

[GC_DDR_TIMING.md](https://github.com/Positron-AI-TSMC/asimov/blob/codex/native-avip-timing/emu/hemi_tlm/doc/GC_DDR_TIMING.md)
details the evidence, assumptions, controls and reset/programming contract.

Validation:

- 106 affected host-side tests passed: 27 timing-configuration, seven structural
  dry-run, four adapter, 25 timed-write, 11 streaming, six streaming-fixture,
  22 staging and four TEL staging cases. Startup tests cover reset overwriting
  early programming, failed initialization, first-operation requirements,
  once-only configuration, unchanged absent settings and malformed source-profile rejection. Dry-run tests cover
  timing profiles, large/repeated loads, scatter, missing/truncated payloads
  and error attribution. Both new regression groups failed against the earlier
  implementation and pass with these changes.
- Host coverage also includes lazy callback registration, retained mapping and
  failure state, operation-buffer boundaries and complete validation before
  target I/O. A 2,051-command group matches the bulk-load AXI request/completion
  trace; the 600,000-command bounded-memory test passed.
- Earlier focused native-AVIP Xcelium qualification passed eight positive runs
  and 27 expected negative controls. Four reproducers confirmed the documented
  Cadence request-limit limitation. Reset restored defaults and cancelled
  outstanding responses; reapplying an override restored the measured 80-cycle
  latency, while omitting reapplication failed the exact-latency assertion.
  Explicit-zero and AUX traces matched native references.
- Earlier reduced XMS/native Xcelium qualification passed three positive
  scenarios and six expected negative controls for payload, partial strobes,
  overlap, shared service, response errors and reset failures. The separate
  C++ TEL collector/checker previously passed 29 positive/negative cases.
- Independent review passed after correcting source-profile validation; whitespace and Python syntax checks passed. The rebase preserved all tested host sources.
  Rebased onto `bdd776f19`. Source manifests and logs for the host changes
  are retained in ws1 under `temp_folder/pr4492-startup-order-20261022/` and
  `temp_folder/pr4492-dryrun-compatibility-20261022/`; earlier native/XMS
  qualification is under `temp_folder/pr4492-timing-reset-20261022/`.
  The latest host changes did not rerun RTL simulation.

Additional post-staging artifact-length validation remains deferred: truncated
sources fail when requested bytes are unavailable, possibly after partial writes,
while oversized artifacts may be accepted. Production IXCOM compilation and
Palladium/MARG qualification remain outstanding; no full-hemisphere or hardware
run was submitted.
title: emu: share Goldcrest AVIP timing with timed host writes
